_comment: Preguntas ORIGINALES tipo NIE del capítulo 1.6. No son preguntas reales del examen. Comprueba con tu edición 2027.

questions.scenario: Officers hear screaming from a flat and get no answer. Which power allows entry?
options: s. 17 PACE – to save life or limb

questions.scenario: For s. 17 entry to arrest a person for an indictable offence, what must the officer believe?
options: That there are reasonable grounds for believing the person sought is on the premises

questions.scenario: Which purpose under s. 17 does NOT require reasonable grounds to believe the person sought is on the premises?
options: Recapturing a person unlawfully at large

questions.scenario: Under s. 17, can officers enter to recapture an escaped prisoner?
options: Yes – a person unlawfully at large whom they are pursuing

questions.scenario: After an arrest for an indictable offence, which premises may be searched under s. 18?
options: Premises occupied or controlled by the arrested person

questions.scenario: Who must authorise a s. 18 search, and how?
options: An inspector or above, in writing

questions.scenario: Under s. 18(5), a search may be carried out before the inspector authorises it when…
options: The arrested person's presence at the premises is necessary for the effective investigation of the offence

questions.scenario: Under s. 18, the evidence sought must relate to…
options: That offence or some other indictable offence connected with or similar to it

questions.scenario: Under s. 32, which premises may be searched?
options: Premises where he was when arrested or immediately before he was arrested
Any premises owned by the arrested person

questions.scenario: Officers return to the arrest address two hours after the arrest to search under s. 32. Following R v Badham…
options: Unlawful – s. 32 searches must be carried out at the time of arrest
Lawful if they had no time

questions.scenario: Under s. 32, a person searched in public can be required to remove…
options: Only outer coat, jacket and gloves (and the mouth may be searched)

questions.scenario: Who issues a search warrant under s. 8 PACE?
Which is NOT a condition for a s. 8 warrant?
options: An indictable offence has been committed
Material likely of substantial value to the investigation
The material includes items subject to legal privilege
The material is likely to be relevant evidence
explanations: Correct – privileged material must NOT be included.

questions.scenario: Within how long must a search warrant be executed?
When executing a warrant with the occupier present, officers must…
options: Identify themselves, show the warrant and give the occupier a copy

questions.scenario: At what time should a warrant normally be executed?
options: At a reasonable hour, unless that might frustrate the purpose of the search

questions.scenario: A victim's hospital medical records are needed. What type of material are they?
options: Excluded material – production order/warrant from a circuit judge (Schedule 1)
explanations: Personal records in confidence are excluded.

questions.scenario: Can items subject to legal privilege be seized?
options: No (unless held with the intention of furthering a criminal purpose)

questions.scenario: Under s. 19, an officer lawfully on premises may seize something if he reasonably believes it is evidence or obtained by an offence AND…
options: It is necessary to seize it to prevent it being concealed, lost, damaged, altered or destroyed

questions.scenario: A computer contains thousands of files, and it isn't practicable to separate relevant ones on the premises. Which power?
Under Code B, how should consent to a search be given where practicable?
options: In writing on the Notice of Powers and Rights

questions.scenario: When searching premises, what must officers do when leaving if the occupier is absent?
options: Leave the premises secure and leave a copy of the Notice/warrant

questions.scenario: Which power is preserved to enter premises to prevent a breach of the peace?
D is arrested for shoplifting (an indictable offence ⚠) outside a car he has just got out of. Can officers search the car under s. 32?
options: Yes – premises (including a vehicle) where he was immediately before arrest, for evidence of that offence
